title: Secret management: keys in the repository and in environment variables

videos.script: A developer pastes a payment key into a settings file, just to try something. {{paste}} The test passes and the commit goes in. A minute later they notice. So they delete the line and commit again. {{delete}} The file is clean now. The key is not gone. It is still in the first commit, in every copy of the repository. {{history}} Deleting it fixed nothing. The fix is to make the key worthless: revoke it, and issue a new one. {{rotate}} In this lesson you make that mistake on purpose, in a throwaway repository, with a key nobody ever issued. {{repo}} You scan the files, and find nothing. You scan the history, and find it at once. {{scan}} You move the key into the environment, and see who can still read it there. {{environ}} And you install a hook that refuses the commit, before the key ever reaches the history. {{hook}}
